setup: Lie on your back on a flat bench and hold the bar with your hands slightly wider than your shoulders.
Press your feet into the floor and your hips into the bench as you lift the bar off the rack.
movement: Lower the bar slowly to your chest, letting your elbows bend out to the sides.
Stop when your elbows are just below the level of the bench.
Press your feet into the floor and push the bar straight back up.

setup: Lie back on an incline bench (the source describes 45 to 60 degrees) with your feet firmly on the floor or a raised platform.
Pull your shoulders down and back against the bench. Keep your head, shoulders, hips and feet in contact throughout.
Press the dumbbells up over your eyes with straight arms, palms facing forward and wrists straight.
movement: Breathe in and lower the dumbbells slowly towards your upper chest, slightly wide towards your armpits, elbows under your wrists.
Breathe out and press back up until your arms are straight.
mistakes: Bouncing the dumbbells off your chest.
Arching your lower back, or lifting your head, hips or feet.
Letting your wrists bend back or forward.

setup: Lie on your back on a flat bench with your feet firmly on the floor.
Pull your shoulders down and back against the bench.
Press the dumbbells up to about eye level with straight arms, palms facing forward and wrists straight.
movement: Breathe in and lower the dumbbells slowly towards the middle of your chest.
Breathe out and press back up until your arms are straight.
mistakes: Bouncing the dumbbells off your chest.
Arching your lower back, or lifting your head, hips or feet.
Letting your wrists bend back or forward.

setup: Hold one dumbbell with both hands around the handle. The source stands in a split stance; the demonstration sits on a bench with a back support.
Brace your middle, pull your shoulders down and back, and keep your head in line with your spine.
Press the dumbbell overhead until your arms are upright, elbows pointing forward and not locked.
movement: Breathe in and let the dumbbell lower slowly behind your head without moving your upper arms.
Stop when your elbows reach about a right angle, or when your upper arms start to move back.
Breathe out and straighten your arms again.
mistakes: Letting your upper arms drift forwards or back.
Touching the back of your head with the dumbbell.
Moving your head, body or feet during the set.
